title: QBR Launchpad + Renewal Playbook (standard & enterprise)
content:
Purpose and scope:
This doc is a compact, reusable QBR deck template and associated renewal-playbook for two common customer tiers: Standard (self-service + lower-touch commercial) and Enterprise (SLA, integrations, exec sponsorship). Use as the single source for slide order, talking points, success metrics, and an embedded renewal-tracker sketch you can copy into a sheet before every meeting.

High-level differences (one-liner):
- Standard: 30–45 min; focus on usage, quick wins, adoption blockers, and one clear CTA (expand or health check).
- Enterprise: 60–90 min; pre-read required; includes technical health, roadmap alignment, ROI case, executive ask, and a Risk + Champion health review.

Run-of-show (templates)
A. Standard QBR (30–45m)
  1) 0–5m: Welcome & agenda (CS lead + AE) — 1 slide
     - Note: set expectations: what we’ll cover and the ask at the end.
  2) 5–12m: Key outcomes since last touch (usage highlights, 2–3 wins) — 1 slide
     - Metrics: active seats/APIs, weekly tokens/month, latency P95, error rate, cost per 1k tokens (if relevant).
  3) 12–25m: Adoption & health (feature adoption funnels, blockers) — 2 slides
     - Call out 1 high-impact adoption opportunity.
  4) 25–35m: Roadmap alignment & short-term plan (next 30–60 days) — 1 slide
  5) 35–40m: Renewal check-in / next steps / clear ask (trial conversion, expansion, pricing discussion) — 1 slide
  6) 40–45m: Action items & close — 1 slide

B. Enterprise QBR (60–90m)
  Pre-work (required 7–14 days before): share data exports (usage, error logs), 1-page ROI template filled by customer, and stakeholder list.
  1) 0–10m: Exec summary & strategic context (customer exec + Redwood exec) — 1 slide
  2) 10–25m: Business outcomes & ROI narrative — 2 slides
     - Show: topline outcomes, cost savings or revenue enablement, ARR impact, and adoption velocity.
  3) 25–40m: Technical health & risk register — 2 slides
     - Observability: latency by region, KV cache hit rate, model fallback events, security incidents (if any).
     - Risk matrix (Impact x Likelihood) with owner and mitigation.
  4) 40–55m: Product roadmap & integration roadmap — 2 slides
     - Where Redwood will invest that affects customer; integration milestones.
  5) 55–70m: Commercial & renewal discussion (AE + CS lead) — 1 slide
     - Renewal timeline, committed vs. forecasted ARR, expansion opportunities.
  6) 70–85m: Action plan & governance (owners, dates, success criteria) — 1 slide
  7) 85–90m: Close & executive asks — 1 slide

Slide bank (bulleted notes you can paste into slides)
- Title slide: Customer name / Redwood CS lead / AE / Date / Quarter
- Agenda: 3 bullets (Outcomes, Health, Ask)
- Topline KPI snapshot: 6 metrics (Active projects, Monthly tokens, Avg latency P95, Error rate %, Cost per 10k tokens, NPS or CSAT) with sparkline last 6 months
- Success story: 2–3 sentences + metric improvement (before/after)
- Adoption funnel: Seats/Integrations/Active Users/Automations — call out drop-off points and root cause hypotheses
- Technical health: incidents (count), mean time to recover (MTTR), model fallbacks, and support SR backlog
- Risk register: short list with owner and due date
- Roadmap alignment: 3 items with impact on customer success
- Renewal slide (commercial): renewal date, current ARR/ACV, recommended motion (renew, expand, modify), target decision date
- Ask slide: 3 clear asks (e.g., approve pilot expansion, provide SSO admin access, confirm renewal authorization)

Renewal tracker (mini-template to paste into sheet)
Columns (one-line headers you can copy):
- customer_name, product_tier, contract_end_date, current_acv, renewal_owner, renewal_stage (discovery|proposal|negotiation|committed), renewal_risk (low|medium|high), champion_name, champion_health (0-10), exec_sponsor (yes|no), next_action, next_action_date, renewal_notes

How to score Champion Health (simple heuristic)
- 8–10: active sponsor, engaged in roadmap, responds within 48 hours
- 5–7: functional contact, attends quarterly calls, sometimes delayed decisions
- 0–4: inactive or changed org, no clear sponsor — label high renewal risk

Renewal Risk Matrix (guidance)
- Low: champion_health >= 8, product adoption trend up, no open P1/P2 incidents, contract timeline >60 days
- Medium: champion_health 5–7 OR one outstanding integration blocker OR some performance issues
- High: champion_health <=4 OR exec sponsor left OR open critical P1 incident OR contract <30 days with stalled commercial conversation

Playbook actions by renewal_stage
- discovery: map stakeholders, collect ROI numbers, confirm renewal timeline, get pre-reads assigned.
- proposal: propose one expansion path (usage, seats, features), internal pricing approval (AE+Finance), send proposal with 10-day feedback window.
- negotiation: be clear on concessions (discount floors), tie concessions to commitments (term length, seats), run legal/finance in parallel.
- committed: schedule kickoff, set success KPIs and a 30/60/90 day plan, invoice and set up billing owners.

Templates (copy/paste snippets)
- Pre-QBR email to customer:
  Subject: Redwood QBR prep — {Customer} — {Quarter} — Data request
  Body: Hi {Name}, we’re preparing the QBR for {Date}. Could you share the 1-page ROI doc (attached), confirm attendees, and provide any additional topics you want on the agenda? Please send by {Date - 7 days}. Thanks, {CS lead}

- Post-QBR follow-up (short):
  Subject: Follow-up & action items — QBR {Customer} {Quarter}
  Body: Thanks for your time today. Attached: deck + action-items. Next action: {owner} will {task} by {date}. Please confirm.

Operational notes & internal checklist (pre-meeting)
- Export usage snapshot (last 90 days), run latency/error queries (SRE view) — attach CSV
- Confirm attendees and send calendar invites with pre-read
- Run security checklist for Enterprise customers (SSO, IP allowlist, SOC artifacts)
- AE: confirm commercial positioning and any open discounts or legal items
- CS: prepare adoption narrative and one clear recommendation

Escalation path (if renewal at risk)
1) CS lead escalates to CS Manager and AE within 48 hours
2) Joint call with Solutions Eng for technical blocker within 72 hours
3) If exec sponsor is needed, request a 15m shadow slot on the next exec sync; prep 1-slide ask and 1-slide ROI

Notes on delivery tone and facilitation
- Standard: brisk, outcomes-focused. Keep slides to 6–8 and allow time for questions.
- Enterprise: collaborative, evidence-first. Encourage customer exec to open with strategic priorities. Use data-heavy appendices for deep dives.

Appendix ideas (for Enterprise only)
- Appendix A: Raw KPI exports (attach CSV filenames)
- Appendix B: Incident timeline & remediation notes
- Appendix C: Integration checklist and open JIRA keys (ex: INTEG-256, INTEG-301)
- Appendix D: Contract snapshot (term, SLA, termination clauses)

Versioning and ownership
- This doc template is owned by CS Enablement. For edits, open a PR on Confluence (confluence:CS-QBR-Launchpad-1234) and tag @Priya Nair.

Quick wins to include in every QBR (small, high-impact asks)
- Two-click suggestion: enable feature X for pilot users (measurable within 30 days)
- One automation: configure a daily usage digest for the champion
- One governance ask: confirm renewal decision maker and timing

Thoughts / open questions (capture during rehearsal)
- Does the AE need to include pricing scenarios for every Standard QBR, or only when expansion is likely?
- For Enterprise customers, should we require an SLA health slide even when there are no incidents?

Copy checklist before you run a QBR
- Duplicate deck from templates folder
- Fill KPI snapshot from analytics exports
- Update renewal tracker row for the customer
- Send pre-read and confirm attendees

End of doc.
